holidays.name: National Umbrella Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble rain-blocking, sun-shading, sidewalk-poking umbrella. Grab your favorite canopy on a stick and give it the appreciation it deserves, whether or not the forecast calls for rain.
holidays.origin: Created as an unofficial observance by Umbrella Day enthusiasts in the United States, reportedly tied to the umbrella's long history as a tool for shade and rain protection. The exact founder is not well documented.
holidays.funFact: Umbrellas were originally used for shade, not rain, and appear in ancient Egyptian, Chinese, and Assyrian art thousands of years ago. In many early cultures, they were status symbols for royalty.

holidays.name: National Cream Cheese Brownie Day
holidays.description: A delicious day for swirling tangy cream cheese into rich chocolate brownies. It is the perfect excuse to bake, buy, or simply inhale a pan of marbled goodness.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday, likely the brainchild of dessert lovers and food-day calendars. No single creator is known.
holidays.funFact: Cream cheese was famously invented by accident in the 1800s in New York when a dairyman was trying to recreate a French cheese called Neufchâtel and produced a richer, creamier version instead.

holidays.name: Plimsoll Day
holidays.description: A nod to the humble load line painted on the sides of ships, which keeps cargo vessels from sinking under too much stuff. It is a salute to the maritime reformer who made shipping safer.
holidays.origin: Celebrated in the UK in honor of Samuel Plimsoll, born February 10, 1824, the politician who campaigned for the Merchant Shipping Act and the mandatory load line, known as the Plimsoll line.
holidays.funFact: Plimsoll shoes, a type of British sneaker, are said to be named after him because the line of the sole's rubber band resembled the Plimsoll line on a ship's hull.

holidays.name: World Pulses Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of lentils, chickpeas, beans, and dry peas, the unsung heroes of protein, fiber, and sustainable farming. Time to give legumes their moment in the spotlight.
holidays.origin: Declared by the United Nations General Assembly in 2018 after the success of the 2016 International Year of Pulses, and observed annually on February 10.
holidays.funFact: Pulses use far less water than many other protein sources and can improve soil by fixing nitrogen, so farmers essentially get free fertilizer from the plants themselves.

holidays.name: Take Your Child to the Library Day Weekend Kickoff Vibes: Dumb Ox Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day honoring the nickname once given to the philosopher Thomas Aquinas, who was teased as a quiet student. It celebrates slow thinkers and late bloomers everywhere.
holidays.origin: Loosely inspired by the story that classmates of Thomas Aquinas called him the Dumb Ox because he was big and silent, until his teacher predicted his bellows of wisdom would echo around the world.
holidays.funFact: Aquinas went on to write the massive Summa Theologica, a work so long that it remained unfinished at his death, proving the quiet kid can absolutely have the last word.
